newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Irish farm minister sees way to ease British beef ban.
newsitem.headline: Irish farm minister sees way to ease British beef ban.

text.p: Irish Farm Minister Ivan Yates said on Wednesday that one way of ending an impasse over easing a British beef export ban would be to carry out a selective cull and perhaps introduce a certified herd scheme for Northern Ireland.
Yates said the Irish EU Presidency had tried to see what support there would be for such a proposal, which would have to come from Britain, during recent contacts with member states.

"The majority of states were sympathetic to something that would limit animal movements between Northern Ireland and the rest of United Kingdom," Yates told a news conference after a three-day meeting of EU farm ministers.

Yates stressed the need to respect an agreement by EU leaders in Florence for a gradual lifting of the ban subject to fulfilment of strict conditions to eradicate the disease, including a selective cull of animals most at risk.
The agreement set out a clear procedure, the first step being for Britain to bring forward a working document on a region of Britain or Northern Ireland, he added.
Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler added that EU scientists must give their support before any decision can be taken by the EU's Standing Veterinary Committee of senior national officials.
"The first move has to be made by the British government," he stressed.
The EU imposed a global ban on British beef exports in March after the British government admitted that the fatal cattle brain disease could be passed to people who ate infected beef.
